phase: P06 (batch 3: cart, checkout and reservation ownership)
scope: All 44 cart, checkout and reservation routes and their guards
application/services/cart-management.service.ts validateCartOwnership; checkout.service.ts and checkout-order.service.ts ownership checks
Storefront and admin use of the reservation API
reviewed_without_change: Every cart-by-id operation (read, summary, add, update, remove, clear, email, shipping, addresses) checks ownership in the service and fails closed.
Guest-token routes treat the token as a bearer secret; admin cart statistics and cleanup are admin-only.

findings.problem: GET/POST/DELETE /users/:userId/cart used the user id from the URL without comparing it to the signed-in user, so any customer could read, create or empty another customer's cart (contents, contact and address details) by user id.
findings.change: Customers may only address their own user id; admins may address any.
findings.verification: cart-ownership E2E: baseline another customer's cart readable and clearable; fixed 403, own cart 200.

findings.problem: Guest-cart transfer only checked the target user when the caller was signed in, so an anonymous caller with a guest token could merge that cart into any account.
findings.change: Transfer requires a signed-in customer and always targets their own account (401 otherwise).
findings.verification: E2E: baseline anonymous transfer accepted; fixed 401 and no cart created for the victim.

findings.problem: Checkout ownership checks only ran for the identity that was supplied ('if userId then compare; if guestToken then compare'), so a request with neither identity skipped them. GET /checkout/:checkoutId has no cart-auth guard, so anyone could read any checkout by id.
findings.change: One fail-closed rule (assertOwnership) for all checkout operations: a customer's checkout needs that customer's session, a guest's needs its token, anything else is refused.
findings.verification: E2E: baseline anonymous read returned the checkout; fixed refused, owner 200. Unit fixtures now supply the owner identity.

findings.problem: The reservation API (create, bulk create, extend, renew, adjust, release, read by cart) was open to every customer with no ownership checks, so a customer could change other carts' reservations or reserve a product's whole stock to make it appear sold out. No storefront code uses it; the cart service manages reservations internally.
findings.change: Reservation routes require ADMIN; public availability and reserved-quantity reads are unchanged.
findings.verification: E2E: baseline customer reservation request accepted past authorisation; fixed 403.

tests.updated: Checkout unit fixtures (stripe-initialization, payment-verification, complete-checkout-race) now complete checkouts as their owner; the cart lifecycle E2E runs its reservation steps as an admin and asserts the customer is refused
tests.baseline: With the old controller, services and routes: 4 of 4 E2E cases failed.
tests.database_suites: All E2E and integration suites: 137 tests in 42 files pass. A first full run had two failures: the cart lifecycle E2E still used the reservation API as a customer (updated, see above) and the user-lifecycle E2E timed out starting the server under load (passes when rerun; the machine had also restarted during the run).
tests.final: 1511 unit tests in 117 files; root/tooling tsc; 7/7 workspace type-checks; API client drift check

follow_ups: Owner decision: checkout tax falls back to a simulated 8% when Stripe Tax fails or returns 0 (production should fail or use configured rates).
CartOwnershipError responds 422; 403 would be the conventional status (left unchanged to avoid client-visible churn).
Promotion application endpoints belong to the payment module and are reviewed in P08.
